hero.lead: A monthly apartment set in a quiet residential neighborhood — away from the tourist strips. Birdsong in the morning, crickets at night, and Wi-Fi that just works.

manifesto.line1: Too long for a hotel, too short for a lease.

story.p1: Puri Liang is not a resort. We have a pool, but it is not an infinity pool, and we are not on the beach. We are a regular residence built for families and colleagues spending a few months on the island.
story.p2: What we focused on instead is the everyday — making sure daily life runs smoothly without surprise bills piling up. Utilities, housekeeping, towel changes, and an on-site laundry service are all bundled into the monthly rate. Hot water around the clock, staff who respond on weekends, and a ground-floor laundry that operates seven days a week.
story.quote: "Too long for a hotel, too short for a lease. We exist to fill that gap."

hero.lead: Not at the center of any tourist area, but at a kind of "crossroads" — easy access in every direction, while sidestepping the worst of Bali's traffic.

crossroads.title1: Not in the middle of a tourist hub —
crossroads.emphasis: in the middle of all of them
crossroads.lead: Sidakarya sits slightly outside Bali's main tourist areas, but lets you reach the major districts in every direction in a relatively short drive.
crossroads.mapCaption: Approximate distances from Puri Liang Residence to the main areas

directions.title: Toward Sanur
directions.body: Close to the newly opened international hospital in the medical special zone, the ferry port for nearby islands (Nusa Lembongan / Penida), and the redeveloping Sanur area. Easy access to healthcare and island hopping during a long stay.

directions.title: Toward Seminyak / Canggu
directions.body: Multiple access roads run toward Seminyak, Canggu, Kuta, and Legian — you can choose your route depending on traffic. Easy for weekend nightlife and beach clubs.

directions.title: Toward Nusa Dua / Uluwatu
directions.body: Close to the toll-road entrance that shortcuts to Nusa Dua, Benoa, and Uluwatu. Kura Kura Island — with its large mall and financial special zone — is also reachable without sitting in traffic.

directions.title: Toward Ubud
directions.body: Near the main road to Ubud — most trips take under an hour. An easy base for weekend day trips and access to yoga, rice terraces, and markets.

around.title: From the building, on foot or by car.
around.lead: We disclose "how many minutes from here" with distance, time, and mode. Including honest travel times to tourist hubs.

items.title: Mertasari Beach (Sanur)
items.detail: 5 mins by car (or 10 mins by bike). Calm waves, famous sunrise spot, perfect for kite surfing and yoga.

items.title: Local Supermarket
items.detail: 10 mins walk or 3 mins drive. Daily necessities, groceries, imports, and local fruits.

items.title: Local warung & cafe
items.detail: 5 min on foot. Breakfast from Rp 25,000, coffee around Rp 18,000.

items.title: Bank Mandiri / ATM
items.detail: 5 min on foot. Visa / Master accepted. Multiple banks and money changers nearby.

items.title: Ngurah Rai Intl. Airport
items.detail: About 25 min by taxi (via bypass or toll road). Airport pickup Rp 200,000.

items.title: Central Ubud
items.detail: 50 min by car. Yoga, markets, rice terraces — great for day trips.

items.title: Kuta / Seminyak / Canggu
items.detail: 30–45 mins by car. For shopping, dining, nightlife, and beach clubs.

items.title: Sanur Center & Harbor
items.detail: 10 min by car. Trendy cafes, dining, and speedboats to Nusa Penida/Lembongan.

neighborhood.lead: The things you only see when you live somewhere — written honestly.

notes.title: Not a tourist area, which matters
notes.body: Sidakarya rarely shows up in guidebooks. That is exactly why the warungs where locals eat breakfast and the squares they gather in the evening are still here. Everyday Bali continues as daily life in this area.

notes.title: On safety
notes.body: It's a residential neighborhood and stays relatively quiet at night. We don't recommend walking alone late, but plenty of women have stayed here long-term solo. Building entrance is always locked, shared areas have cameras.

notes.title: Cost of living
notes.body: A meal at a local warung is Rp 25,000–50,000 (about US $1.50–3) — roughly half of tourist-area prices. Cooking at home from the supermarket is cheaper still. Some residents keep monthly food costs under US $200.

notes.title: Getting around
notes.body: Motorbike rental (Rp 800,000/month) is the norm. If you're not used to riding, Grab / Gojek (Bali's Uber) is convenient — they pick up right at the building.

items.a: Rent + Wi-Fi + utilities in shared areas + weekly housekeeping + twice-weekly towel change. Only electricity is billed at actual usage (roughly Rp 600,000–1,200,000 / month per room). Prices are based on Indonesian Rupiah (IDR); JPY and USD displays are approximate.
We accept stays from 1 month. Continuous stays of 3+ months are 10% off, 6+ months are 15% off.
Bank transfer (JPY / USD), Wise, Revolut, and Wise Business are supported. Initial payment is 1 month + Rp 2,000,000 deposit at booking.
Up to 2 weeks before check-in: 50% refund. Up to 1 week before: 25% refund. After that: non-refundable.
No pets. Strict no-smoking indoors; designated outdoor areas only.
Download 80–150 Mbps, upload 50–100 Mbps. Stable across the building and every room.
Check-in from 14:00, check-out by 11:00. Please ask about early / late arrangements.

items.q: How do I get here from the airport?
items.a: About 1 hr 30 min by car from Ngurah Rai International Airport (up to 2 hrs in traffic). Pickup available (Rp 350,000) or Grab/Gojek (around Rp 250,000).
Villa has a full kitchen (stove, fridge, microwave, cookware, dishware). Studios have a mini kitchen (microwave, fridge, kettle, basic dishware).
An on-site laundry service operates on the ground floor, available seven days a week. The twice-weekly towel change is included in the monthly rate.
General clinic 5 min by car. Siloam Hospitals (international hospital) 30 min by car — English-speaking, cashless insurance accepted. Staff help arrange transport in emergencies.
Yes, with advance notice (free). Overnight visitors are Rp 200,000 per night, up to 3 nights. Shared areas are open to all residents.
